historic/u1e4/burgesses-assembly.jpg.description: The first House of Burgesses assembly at Jamestown, 1619 (Armstrong illustration, public domain).

historic/u1e4/delaware-portrait.jpg.description: Thomas West, 3rd Baron De La Warr (Lord Delaware), 1605 portrait — governor who saved Jamestown in 1610.

historic/u1e4/james-i.jpg.description: James VI and I of England, portrait by Paul van Somer — granted the Virginia Company charter; author of A Counterblaste to Tobacco.

historic/u1e4/james-river-map.jpg.description: Captain John Smith's 1612/1624 map of Virginia, showing Chesapeake Bay and the James River — used for the three-ships MapJourney.

historic/u1e4/john-smith.jpg.description: Captain John Smith, c.1617 engraving (National Portrait Gallery, after Simon van de Passe). CC0 dedication.

historic/u1e4/pocahontas-real.jpg.description: The real Pocahontas (Matoaka/Rebecca Rolfe), 1616 engraving by Simon van de Passe — the only lifetime portrait. NOT Disney.

historic/u1e4/powhatan-village.jpg.description: The 1622 Powhatan attack on the English settlements near Jamestown — engraving in the style of Theodor de Bry (Matthäus Merian tradition).

historic/u1e4/starving-time.jpg.description: Bleak winter landscape (Bruegel, Hunters in the Snow, 1565) — dark visual for the Starving Time, winter 1609-1610.

historic/u1e4/three-ships.jpg.description: The three Jamestown replica ships (Susan Constant, Godspeed, Discovery) sailing the James River, 2007 US Navy photo.

historic/u1e4/tobacco-curing.jpg.description: Workers cutting tobacco and loading sticks for the curing/drying barn (1939 FSA/OWI photo, public domain — process shown is centuries-old, though photo is modern).

historic/u1e4/tobacco-plant.jpg.description: Nicotiana tabacum (tobacco plant) botanical illustration from Köhler's Medizinal-Pflanzen (1887, public domain).

historic/u1e4/virginia-company.jpg.description: Seal of the Virginia Company of London.

historic/u1e4/white-lion-ship.jpg.description: 17th-century Dutch armed merchantman/privateer by Wenceslaus Hollar (Rijksmuseum) — representative of the White Lion, the Dutch privateer that brought the first Africans to Virginia in 1619. CC0.
